content.text:
Using brainstorming, um die Desktop-App zuerst sauber zu spezifizieren.

Der Workspace ist praktisch leer (nur `hello-entire.md`) — also Greenfield. Bestehende Projekte wie [desbma/gotify-desktop](https://github.com/desbma/gotify-desktop) sind eher Tray-/Notification-Daemons ohne Management-UI.

Eine zentrale Frage zuerst:

**Was meinst du mit „Gotify Management via Web-Interface“?**

**A)** Gotify-Server-Web-UI in einem App-Fenster einbetten (WebView auf deine Server-URL) — Apps, Clients, Messages verwalten wie im Browser  
**B)** Eigene schlanke Desktop-UI (Einstellungen, Status, ggf. Nachrichtenliste); Management nur per Link zur Gotify-Web-UI im Browser  
**C)** Eigenes Management-UI in der App (Apps/Clients/Messages selbst nachbauen, ohne Gotify-Web-UI)

Meine Empfehlung wäre **A**: wenig Eigenaufwand, volle Gotify-Funktionen, Tray + native Notifications bleiben in Go.

Welche Variante soll es sein?

<timestamp>Friday, Oct 30, 2026, 1:39 PM (UTC+1)</timestamp>
<user_query>
A)
</user_query>

Passt — eingebettete Gotify-Web-UI.

Nächste Frage zur Nutzung:

**Wie soll sich die App im Alltag verhalten?**

**A)** Tray-first: läuft im Hintergrund, zeigt Notifications; Fenster (Gotify-Web-UI) öffnet sich nur bei Klick aufs Tray-Icon bzw. „Öffnen“  
**B)** Fenster-first: beim Start erscheint die Gotify-Web-UI; Schließen minimiert ins Tray (App bleibt aktiv)  
**C)** Beides wählbar: Startverhalten (Tray vs. Fenster) in den Einstellungen

Empfehlung: **B** — vertraut wie ein normaler Desktop-Client, Notifications + Tray bleiben trotzdem aktiv.

<timestamp>Friday, Oct 30, 2026, 1:40 PM (UTC+1)</timestamp>
<user_query>
B)
</user_query>

Fenster-first ist klar.

Nächste Frage — wichtig für die Architektur, weil die Web-UI und die Notifications unterschiedlich authentifizieren:

**Wie soll die Verbindung eingerichtet werden?**

*(Gotify-Web-UI: Login mit User/Passwort. Desktop-Notifications: Client-Token für den WebSocket `/stream`.)*

**A)** Setup-Dialog: Server-URL + Client-Token eingeben (Token manuell in der Gotify-UI anlegen)  
**B)** Setup-Dialog: Server-URL + Username/Passwort — App legt Client-Token per API selbst an und speichert ihn  
**C)** Beides: Token manuell *oder* per Login erzeugen

Empfehlung: **B** — weniger Reibung beim ersten Start; Token lokal speichern, Passwort nicht dauerhaft halten.

<timestamp>Friday, Oct 30, 2026, 1:40 PM (UTC+1)</timestamp>
<user_query>
B)
</user_query>

Login mit Token-Anlage ist klar. Damit reichen die Anforderungen für die Architekturwahl.

**Drei Ansätze:**

### 1) Wails v2 (WebView) + externes Tray *(Empfehlung)*
Go-Backend für Setup, Token, WebSocket `/stream`, Notifications; Fenster lädt die Gotify-Server-URL. Tray über `fyne-io/systray` o.ä. (Wails v2 hat kein natives Tray).
- **Plus:** Gute Cross-Platform-WebView, Wails-Notifications, klare Go↔UI-Bindings für Setup
- **Minus:** Tray nicht first-party; etwas schwerer Build

### 2) Leichtgewicht: `webview` + `systray` + `beeep`
Kein volles App-Framework — nur die Bausteine.
- **Plus:** Schlank, Tray/Notifications direkt
- **Minus:** Mehr Plattform-Kleinkram, schwächere Dev-Experience als Wails

### 3) Fyne-nativ
Eigene UI in Fyne, Gotify-Web nur im externen Browser.
- **Plus:** Echtes Tray in Fyne
- **Minus:** Widerspricht Variante A (eingebettete Web-UI) — fällt damit aus

**Empfehlung: Ansatz 1 (Wails v2).** Passt zu eingebetteter Gotify-UI, Fenster-first und Login-Setup; Tray und Notifications sind lösbar.

Soll ich das Design auf **Ansatz 1** ausarbeiten?

<timestamp>Friday, Oct 30, 2026, 1:41 PM (UTC+1)</timestamp>
<user_query>
1)
</user_query>
Gut — Ansatz 1. Hier der erste Design-Block: Architektur.

### Architektur (Überblick)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph app [Gotify Desktop App]
    UI[Wails Fenster]
    Setup[Setup Screen]
    Tray[System Tray]
    Core[Go Core]
    Stream[WebSocket Client]
    Notify[Native Notifications]
  end

  Gotify[Gotify Server]
  OS[OS Notification Center]

  Setup -->|"URL + User/Pass"| Core
  Core -->|"POST /client Token anlegen"| Gotify
  Core -->|Token speichern| Config[(lokale Config)]
  UI -->|lädt Server-URL| Gotify
  Stream -->|"GET /stream?token=..."| Gotify
  Stream --> Notify --> OS
  Tray -->|Fenster zeigen / Beenden| UI
  Core --> Tray
  Core --> Stream
```

**Kernidee:** Eine Wails-v2-App mit zwei UI-Zuständen — Setup (eigene schlanke Seite) und danach die eingebettete Gotify-Web-UI. Der Go-Core hält dauerhaft den WebSocket, zeigt Notifications und steuert das Tray. Fenster-schließen = ins Tray minimieren, nicht beenden.

**Module im Go-Core:**
- `config` — Server-URL, Client-Token (kein Passwort dauerhaft)
- `auth` — Login per Basic Auth, Client anlegen
- `stream` — WebSocket mit Reconnect + Catch-up
- `notify` — Wails Notifications API
- `tray` — `fyne-io/systray` (Menü: Öffnen, Einstellungen, Beenden)

Passt dieser Architektur-Rahmen so weit?

<timestamp>Friday, Oct 30, 2026, 1:41 PM (UTC+1)</timestamp>
<user_query>
passt
</user_query>

### Komponenten & Datenfluss

**1. Erster Start / Setup**
- App zeigt lokalen Setup-Screen (Wails-Frontend): Server-URL, Username, Passwort
- Go `auth`: `GET /current/user` (oder Login) mit Basic Auth prüfen → `POST /client` mit Name z.B. `gotify-desktop-<hostname>` → Token speichern
- Passwort nur transient im Speicher, nie in der Config
- Danach: Fenster navigiert zur Server-URL (Gotify-Web-UI); User loggt sich dort normal ein fürs Management

**2. Laufender Betrieb**
- `stream` verbindet zu `wss://…/stream?token=…` (bzw. `ws://`)
- Neue Messages → native Notification (Titel + Body, Priority wenn sinnvoll mappbar)
- Tray: Status (verbunden/getrennt), „Fenster öffnen“, „Einstellungen“, „Beenden“
- Fenster-X / Close: `Hide()` statt Quit; Quit nur über Tray „Beenden“

**3. Config (lokal)**
- Pfad plattformüblich (`~/.config/gotify-desktop/config.json` bzw. AppData / Application Support)
- Inhalt: `server_url`, `client_token`, optionale Flags (z.B. `min_priority`)
- „Einstellungen“ im Tray öffnet wieder den Setup-Screen (URL änderbar, Re-Login möglich → neuer Token)

**4. Frontend-Zustände**
- `setup` — eigene HTML/CSS/JS-Seite
- `gotify` — WebView zeigt Remote-URL (kein iframe-Hack nötig: Navigation bzw. separates Embedded-Browser-Verhalten über Wails Window URL / Frontend-Bridge)

Passt dieser Block? Als Nächstes: Fehlerbehandlung & MVP-Abgrenzung.

# Gotify Desktop App (Wails v2)

## Ziel

Desktop-Client für Gotify (Windows, Linux, macOS) mit:

- Fenster-first: Gotify-Web-UI eingebettet; Schließen minimiert ins Tray
- Setup per Server-URL + Username/Passwort → App legt Client-Token an (Passwort nicht speichern)
- Dauerhafte WebSocket-Verbindung zu `/stream` → native OS-Notifications
- Tray-Menü: Fenster öffnen, Einstellungen, Beenden

## Tech-Stack (festgelegt)

- **Wails v2** (Go + WebView)
- **Tray:** `fyne.io/systray` (Wails v2 hat kein natives Tray)
- **Notifications:** Wails `runtime` Notifications API
- **WebSocket:** `gorilla/websocket` (oder `coder/websocket`) gegen Gotify `/stream`
- **Config:** JSON unter plattformüblichem User-Config-Pfad

## Projektstruktur

```
gotify-desktop/
  main.go                 # Wails entry, OnStartup/OnBeforeClose
  app.go                  # App-Bindings (Connect, GetStatus, OpenSettings, …)
  internal/config/        # Laden/Speichern (server_url, client_token, min_priority)
  internal/auth/          # Basic Auth prüfen, POST /client
  internal/stream/        # WebSocket, Reconnect, Message-Events
  internal/notify/        # Wails-Notifications wrappen
  internal/tray/          # Systray-Menü + Fenster show/hide
  frontend/               # Setup-UI (HTML/CSS/JS oder Vite-Vanilla)
  build/                  # Icons (App + Tray)
  README.md
```

## Kernflüsse

### Setup / Auth

1. Kein gültiger Token → Setup-Screen im Frontend
2. User gibt URL, Username, Passwort ein → Go `Connect(url, user, pass)`
3. Normalisierte Base-URL; Erreichbarkeit + Auth prüfen (`GET /current/user` mit Basic Auth)
4. `POST /client` mit Name `gotify-desktop-<hostname>` → Token in Config speichern
5. Passwort verwerfen; UI wechselt zu Gotify-Remote-URL im WebView
6. Stream-Client starten

### Betrieb

- Stream: `ws(s)://host/stream?token=…`, exponential backoff bei Disconnect
- Nach Reconnect: optional letzte Messages nachziehen (`GET /message?limit=…` seit letzter ID), nur neue als Notification
- Notification: Title + Message-Body; Priority unter `min_priority` überspringen
- Close-Button: `OnBeforeClose` → Fenster verstecken, `return true` (App läuft weiter)
- Tray „Beenden“: Stream stoppen, wirklich quitten

### Gotify-Web-UI einbetten

- Nach Setup: Fenster-Inhalt auf konfigurierte Server-URL umleiten (Wails-Frontend navigiert bzw. lädt Remote; falls Same-Origin/StartURL-Limits: dedizierte „shell“-Seite mit Vollflächen-Navigation über Binding `GetServerURL` + `window.location` / Browser-Open nur als Fallback dokumentieren)
- Konkrete Umsetzung: lokale Shell-Seite mit Hinweis + primär `runtime.BrowserOpenURL` vermeiden; Ziel ist In-App-WebView. Wenn Remote-Navigation in Wails-StartURL eingeschränkt ist: WebView über Frontend `iframe`/`webview`-äquivalent mit Server-URL als `src` (Gotify erlaubt Einbettung prüfen; sonst Window-Navigation auf External URL in Dev/Build absichern)

**Festgelegte Lösung:** Frontend nach erfolgreichem Connect setzt `window.location.href = serverUrl` (volle Navigation des WebViews zur Gotify-UI). Setup erneut über Tray „Einstellungen“: lokales Frontend neu laden (`runtime.WindowExecJS` / App-Restart des Frontend-Assets) bzw. Binding `ShowSetup()` lädt wieder die lokalen Assets.

## Fehlerbehandlung

- Ungültige Credentials / unerreichbarer Server → Fehlermeldung im Setup, kein Token speichern
- Token ungültig (401 am Stream) → Tray-Status „Fehler“, Setup öffnen
- Offline / Suspend → automatischer Reconnect; Tray zeigt „Getrennt“ / „Verbunden“
- Notification-Permission (macOS) → beim Start anfordern; bei Ablehnung im Tray Hinweis
- Self-signed TLS: MVP mit Standard-TLS-Verify; Option `insecure_skip_verify` bewusst **nicht** im MVP (später möglich)

## MVP-Scope (inkl.)

- Setup, Token-Persistenz, Stream, Notifications, Tray, Close→Tray, eingebettete Gotify-UI, Cross-Compile-Doku
- Tray-Status, min_priority in Config (Default 0)

## Explizit nicht im MVP

- Autostart mit OS
- Multi-Server
- Eigene Nachrichtenliste neben Gotify-UI
- Auto-Delete empfangener Messages
- Code-Signing/Notarisierung-Pipeline

## Build & Plattformen

- `wails build` für linux/windows/darwin
- README: Voraussetzungen (Linux: `libgtk-3`, `libwebkit2gtk`; Windows: WebView2; macOS: Xcode CLT)
- Ein gemeinsames Tray-/App-Icon (PNG/ICO/ICNS im `build`-Ordner)

## Teststrategie

- Unit-Tests: `config`, URL-Normalisierung, Message-Filter (`min_priority`)
- Manuell: Setup gegen lokalen Gotify, Notification, Tray Show/Hide/Quit, Reconnect (Server kurz stoppen)

## Umsetzungsreihenfolge

1. Wails-Projekt scaffolden + Modulstruktur
2. Config + Auth + Stream (ohne UI testbar)
3. Setup-Frontend + Bindings
4. Notifications + Tray + Close-Verhalten
5. Remote-Navigation zur Gotify-UI
6. README + Build-Hinweise

### Gotify-Web-UI einbetten

Wails v2 ist nicht als Remote-URL-Wrapper gedacht (`window.location` auf externe Hosts bricht die App-Bindings). Deshalb:

**Festgelegte Lösung:** Lokales Frontend bleibt die Shell. Nach Connect zeigt eine Vollflächen-`iframe`-Ansicht die Gotify-Server-URL. Tray „Einstellungen“ blendet die Setup-Ansicht wieder ein (iframe ausblenden). Falls Gotify `X-Frame-Options`/`CSP frame-ancestors` das Einbetten blockiert: Proxy über Wails `AssetServer`-Middleware (Same-Origin) — im MVP zuerst iframe, bei Blockade Proxy nachziehen.

input.contents:
Gotify Desktop

Connect to your Gotify server. A client token is created automatically; your password is not stored.

# Gotify Desktop

Cross-platform Gotify desktop client built with [Wails v2](https://wails.io) and Go.

## Features

- Connect with Gotify username/password; the app creates a **client token** (password is not stored)
- Native desktop **notifications** via Gotify WebSocket `/stream`
- **System tray** with open / settings / quit
- Window close minimizes to tray (quit only from tray)
- Embedded Gotify **web UI** (management) in an in-app iframe

## Requirements

| Platform | Prerequisites |
|----------|----------------|
| Linux | Go 1.23+, Node.js 18+, `libgtk-3-dev`, `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` (or 4.0), `gcc`, `pkg-config` |
| Windows | Go 1.23+, Node.js 18+, WebView2 runtime |
| macOS | Go 1.23+, Node.js 18+, Xcode Command Line Tools |

Install the Wails CLI:

```bash
go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest
```

## Develop

```bash
cd frontend && npm install && cd ..
wails dev
```

## Build

```bash
wails build
```

Binary output: `build/bin/gotify-desktop` (extension varies by OS).

Cross-compile examples (host toolchains / Docker may be required):

```bash
wails build -platform windows/amd64
wails build -platform darwin/universal
wails build -platform linux/amd64
```

## Configuration

Settings are stored under the user config directory:

- Linux: `~/.config/gotify-desktop/config.json`
- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/gotify-desktop/config.json`
- Windows: `%AppData%\gotify-desktop\config.json`

Fields: `server_url`, `client_token`, `min_priority` (default `0`), `last_message_id`.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

input.contents:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GO_VERSION: "1.25.x"
  NODE_VERSION: "20"
  NODE_OPTIONS: "--max-old-space-size=4096"

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: go test ./...

  build:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.name }})
    needs: test
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: linux-amd64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            platform: linux/amd64
            wails_tags: webkit2_41
            artifact: gotify-desktop
          - name: windows-amd64
            os: windows-latest
            platform: windows/amd64
            wails_tags: ""
            artifact: gotify-desktop.exe
          - name: darwin-universal
            os: macos-latest
            platform: darwin/universal
            wails_tags: ""
            artifact: gotify-desktop.app

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev

      - name: Install Wails CLI
        run: go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@v2.17.0

      - name: Build
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          TAGS_ARG=()
          if [[ -n "${{ matrix.wails_tags }}" ]]; then
            TAGS_ARG=(-tags "${{ matrix.wails_tags }}")
          fi
          # Clear project build:tags on non-Linux so webkit2_41 is not forced elsewhere.
          if [[ "${{ runner.os }}" != "Linux" ]]; then
            # portable edit without relying on jq being present everywhere
            python3 - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          path = Path("wails.json")
          data = json.loads(path.read_text())
          data.pop("build:tags", None)
          path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n")
          PY
          fi
          wails build -platform "${{ matrix.platform }}" -clean "${TAGS_ARG[@]}"

      - name: Package macOS app
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        working-directory: build/bin
        run: |
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent gotify-desktop.app \
            "gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}.zip"

      - name: Prepare Linux artifact
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp "build/bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}" "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}"
          chmod +x "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}"

      - name: Prepare Windows artifact
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp "build/bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}" "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}.exe"

      - name: Prepare macOS artifact
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          mv "build/bin/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}.zip" "dist/"

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    name: Release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Download all build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: release-assets
          pattern: gotify-desktop-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: release-assets/*
          generate_release_notes: true
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

input.new_string:
Ubuntu 24.04 example (`libwebkit2gtk-4.1`):

```bash
sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev
```

### Linux system tray (AppIndicator)

On Linux the tray icon is provided by [`fyne.io/systray`](https://github.com/fyne-io/systray). Unlike Windows and macOS, most Linux desktops do **not** draw tray icons themselves. Instead the app registers a **Status Notifier Item** (SNI) / **AppIndicator** on D-Bus, and a panel applet (or extension) displays it.

If that host component is missing, the app can still run, but:

- no Gotify tray icon appears
- “minimize to tray” feels like the window simply vanished
- Quit / Settings / Open are only reachable via the window menu (where available)

#### Runtime package

On Debian/Ubuntu and derivatives, install the Ayatana AppIndicator library (used by many trays and by Go systray bindings):

```bash
sudo apt install libayatana-appindicator3-1
```

Related packages you may already have via the desktop:

| Package | Role |
|---------|------|
| `libayatana-appindicator3-1` | Runtime library the tray client talks to |
| `libayatana-appindicator3-dev` | Only needed if you **build** against AppIndicator headers |
| `gir1.2-ayatanaappindicator3-0.1` | GObject introspection (often pulled in automatically) |

Older docs mention `libappindicator3-1` (Unity-era). Prefer **Ayatana** on modern Ubuntu; it is the maintained fork.

Fedora / RHEL-like:

```bash
sudo dnf install libappindicator-gtk3
```

Arch:

```bash
sudo pacman -S libappindicator-gtk3
```

#### Desktop environment support

Having the library installed is necessary but not always sufficient. The shell must also **host** indicators:

| Desktop | Tray support |
|---------|----------------|
| **KDE Plasma** | Built-in system tray; works out of the box with SNI |
| **XFCE** | Panel → add “Status Tray Plugin” / “Indicator Plugin” |
| **MATE** | Panel → “Notification Area” / “Indicator Applet Complete” |
| **Cinnamon** | Usually works with the default panel tray |
| **GNOME (45+)** | No classic tray by default. Install an extension such as [AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support](https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/615/appindicator-support/) (`gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` on Ubuntu) and enable it |
| **WSL / headless** | Often **no** tray host at all; run under a full Linux desktop session or WSLg with a DE that provides one |

Ubuntu GNOME example:

```bash
sudo apt install libayatana-appindicator3-1 gnome-shell-extension-appindicator
```

Then enable the extension (Extensions app, or GNOME Tweaks / `gnome-extensions enable …`), and log out/in if the icon still does not show.

#### Build vs run

- **Building** Gotify Desktop needs GTK/WebKit **dev** packages (`libgtk-3-dev`, `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`, …).
- **Running** a prebuilt binary on another machine needs the **runtime** stack: GTK 3, WebKitGTK, and for the tray typically `libayatana-appindicator3-1` plus a working panel indicator host.

#### Quick checks

```bash
# Library present?
ldconfig -p | grep -i appindicator

# Session bus available? (required for StatusNotifierItem)
echo "$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS"

# On GNOME: is the AppIndicator extension enabled?
gnome-extensions list 2>/dev/null | grep -i indicator || true
```

If the window opens but the tray icon never appears, install the Ayatana package, confirm your DE hosts indicators (especially on GNOME), then restart the app.

Install the Wails CLI (ensure `$HOME/go/bin` is on your `PATH`):

```bash
go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@latest
```

Dein Log war der entscheidende Hinweis: **Stream und Notify-API waren OK** — Windows hat den Toast nur nicht angezeigt.

### Ursachen
1. **Login weg:** Bei jedem „Stream connected“ wurde das iframe neu geladen → Gotify-Session kaputt.
2. **Kein Toast:** Unter Windows meldet Wails/WinRT bei ungepackten Apps oft „sent“, ohne sichtbaren Toast ([fehlende Start-Menü-AUMID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/notifications/app-notifications/send-local-toast-other-apps)).

### Fix in **v0.1.4**
- iframe bleibt nach dem ersten Öffnen stehen  
- Windows-Toasts über PowerShell-AUMID (zuverlässiger für ungepackte `.exe`)  
- Proxy setzt Session-Cookie + Token-Injection in die UI  

Release: https://github.com/elpatron68/gotify-desktop/releases/tag/v0.1.4

Beide Symptome haben echte Ursachen — Fixes sind lokal fertig (noch nicht committed).

**Erneutes Einloggen (Gotify 3.1.1)**  
Die UI speichert die Session nur noch als **HttpOnly-Cookie**, nicht in `localStorage`. Unter `/g/` leitet Gotify die API-Basis aus dem Pfad ab; WebSocket/Auth waren fehleranfällig.  
→ Loopback-Server `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (Gotify unter `/`), HttpOnly-Session-Cookie, Auth-Header + `?token=` am Stream.

**Keine sichtbare Notification**  
`windows toast sent` heißt nur: PowerShell/`Show` ohne Fehler — bei unpackaged Apps oft **ohne sichtbaren Toast**, wenn keine eigene AUMID registriert ist.  
→ Registry-AUMID `Gotify.Desktop`, `SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID`, Startmenü-Shortcut, Versand über `go-toast`.

Zum Testen: committen, pushen, taggen (z. B. `v0.1.5`), Windows-Build aus CI holen. Soll ich commit + Tag machen?

func extractScript(html string) string {
	i := strings.Index(html, "<script>(function")
	if i < 0 {
		return "(none)"
	}
	j := strings.Index(html[i:], "</script>")
	if j < 0 {
		return html[i:min(i+120, len(html))]
	}
	s := html[i : i+j+9]
	if len(s) > 180 {
		return s[:180] + "…"
	}
	return s

content.text:
## Befunde (mit deinem Token gegen https://gotify.elpatron.me)

| Check | Ergebnis |
|--------|----------|
| Token (`X-Gotify-Key` / Bearer / Cookie / Query) | alles **200** |
| Proxy `/g/current/user` mit Auth-Injection | **200** |
| Proxy-HTML-Bootstrap | setzt Cookie + **WebSocket-Rewrite** |

Das Token und der HTTP-Proxy waren also nicht das Problem.

## Eigentliche Ursachen

**1. Erneutes Login**

- Wails AssetServer gibt für WebSockets **501** zurück ([Wails-Doku/Code](https://github.com/wailsapp/wails/blob/master/v2/pkg/assetserver/assetserver.go)).
- Gotify unter `/g/` kann HTTP-Auth, aber `ws://…/g/stream` scheitert.
- v0.1.5 wich auf `http://127.0.0.1:…` aus — WebView2 blockiert das oft (Local Network Access).
- Zusätzlich: Gotify ruft bei 4xx `logout()` auf → **löscht den Desktop-Client** → Stream tot → Setup-Maske.

**2. Kein Toast**

- `Show()` / COM meldet Erfolg, ohne dass etwas sichtbar wird (unpackaged App ohne wirksame AUMID-Bindung). Unser Code hat diesen „Erfolg“ als fertig gewertet.

## Fix (lokal, noch nicht committed)

- UI wieder **same-origin `/g/`**
- Inject: WebSocket → `wss://gotify.elpatron.me/stream?token=…`
- `POST /auth/logout` im Proxy = No-Op (Client bleibt)
- Kein Auto-Open der Setup-Maske mehr bei Stream-401
- Toasts: explizites PowerShell + AUMID-Registrierung

Live verifiziert: Inject enthält `window.WebSocket` + `wss://gotify.elpatron.me` + `stream?token=`, `/current/user` → 200.

Bitte das Client-Token **widerrufen** (Clients in Gotify), es stand im Chat.

Soll ich committen, pushen und als **v0.1.6** taggen?

<user_query>
"Optional: sag kurz, ob „erneutes Login“ die Desktop-Connect-Maske oder die Gotify-Login-Seite im iframe ist."

Gotify-Login-Seite im iframe
</user_query>

Das passt zur Diagnose: Die Gotify-SPA lädt, aber `tryAuthenticate()` → `GET …/current/user` scheitert (4xx) bzw. danach greift `logout()` — deshalb die Login-Seite im iframe, nicht unsere Connect-Maske.

Genau dagegen zielt der aktuelle Fix:
- Session über den `/g/`-Proxy mit Token-Injection
- WebSocket direkt zum Server (`wss://…/stream?token=…`), weil Wails kein WS kann
- Logout im Proxy als No-Op, damit der Desktop-Client nicht gelöscht wird

# Gotify Android Build Status FOSSA Status latest release version F-Droid

Gotify Android connects to gotify/server and shows push notifications on new messages.

## Features

* show push notifications on new messages
* view and delete messages

## Installation

Download the apk or get the app via F-Droid or Google Play.

Get it on Google Play Get it on F-Droid Get it on F-Droid

Google Play and the Google Play logo are trademarks of Google LLC.

### Disable battery optimization

By default Android kills long running apps as they drain the battery. With enabled battery optimization, Gotify will be killed and you wont receive any notifications.

Here is one way to disable battery optimization for Gotify.

* Open "Settings"
* Search for "Battery Optimization"
* Find "Gotify" and disable battery optimization

See also <https://dontkillmyapp.com> for phone manufacturer specific instructions to disable battery optimizations.

### Minimize the Gotify foreground notification

_Only possible for Android version >= 8_

The foreground notification showing the connection status can be manually minimized to be less intrusive:

* Open Settings -> Apps -> Gotify
* Click Notifications
* Click on `Gotify foreground notification`
* Toggle the "Minimize" option / Select a different "Behavior" or "Importance" (depends on your Android version)
* Restart Gotify

## Message Priorities

| Notification                                 | Gotify Priority |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| \-                                           | 0               |
| Icon in notification bar                     | 1 - 3           |
| Icon in notification bar + Sound             | 4 - 7           |
| Icon in notification bar + Sound + Vibration | 8 - 10          |

## Building

Use Java 17 and execute the following command to build the apk.

$ ./gradlew build

## Update client

* Run `./gradlew openApiGenerate`
* Commit changes

| Speichert `url` + `username` + `token`, nie Passwort | ebenso (`config.json`) |

| Native OS-Notifications | Toast-Versuche + Tray-Hinweis + Fenster nach vorne |
| Eigenes Logging | `desktop.log` zusätzlich zu `notify.log` |

Passwort wird bewusst **nicht** gespeichert (wie Android).

content.text:
Ja — und bei euch ist schon Vorarbeit da: CI liefert aktuell nur Binaries/Zip, aber unter `build/windows/installer/` liegen bereits Wails-NSIS-Templates.

## Kurzempfehlung

| Plattform | Pragmatisch (schnell) | „Store/Distribution“ |
|-----------|----------------------|----------------------|
| **Windows** | **NSIS** (`wails build -nsis`) | MSI/MSIX nur bei Store/Enterprise-Bedarf |
| **Linux** | **AppImage** (+ optional `.deb`) | Flatpak (Flathub) separat, mehr Aufwand |
| **macOS** | **`.app` + DMG** (ggf. Zip wie jetzt) | Notarisierung + Signing für fremde Macs |

---

## Windows: MSI vs. Inno Setup / NSIS

**NSIS ist der natürliche Fit** für Wails v2:

```bash
wails build -platform windows/amd64 -nsis
```

Voraussetzung: `makensis` auf dem Runner (`choco install nsis` / `winget install NSIS.NSIS`). Eure `project.nsi` / `wails_tools.nsh` sind schon da; in `wails.json` solltet ihr noch einen `info`-Block (ProductName, Version, Company…) pflegen — den zieht der Installer.

**Inno Setup** geht auch (eigenes `.iss`), bringt aber keinen Vorteil gegenüber dem bereits integrierten NSIS.

**MSI** (WiX): möglich, aber Extra-Tooling und Wartung. Für eine Desktop-Tray-App meist unnötig. **MSIX** eher Store/Managed-Deploy — in Wails v3 stärker vorgesehen, bei v2 eher manuell.

Zusätzlich lohnt **Code Signing** (sonst SmartScreen-Warnungen bei Download von GitHub).

---

## Linux: AppImage & Flatpak

**AppImage** — gut geeignet:
- Binary + `.desktop` + Icon in ein `AppDir`, dann `appimagetool`
- Passt zu eurem einen Executable + WebKitGTK-Abhängigkeit (AppImage kann Libs bundlen oder auf System-WebKit setzen — bundlen ist robuster, Image größer)

**`.deb`** — sinnvoll parallel (Ubuntu/Debian), einfacher als Flatpak, gut für Releases.

**Flatpak** — ja, aber:
- eigenes Manifest, Runtime (`org.gnome.Platform` o.ä.), oft Portal-Themen für Tray/Notifications
- Systray/AppIndicator unter Flatpak ist historisch hakelig
- Flathub-Review-Prozess

Für den Start: **AppImage + optional deb**; Flatpak erst, wenn ihr Flathub wirklich wollt.

---

## macOS: Was passt?

Standard und richtig:

1. **`gotify-desktop.app`** — macht `wails build` bereits (CI zippt das)
2. **DMG** als „Installer-Feeling“:

```bash
hdiutil create -volname "Gotify Desktop" \
  -srcfolder build/bin/gotify-desktop.app \
  -ov -format UDZO Gotify-Desktop.dmg
```

Optional schöner mit `create-dmg`.

Ohne **Apple Developer ID + Notarisierung** bekommen fremde Nutzer Gatekeeper-Warnungen („unbekanntes Entwickler“). Für echte Distribution ist das der eigentliche Aufwand, nicht das DMG-Format.

Universal Binary (amd64+arm64) wäre nice-to-have; aktuell baut ihr nur `darwin/arm64`.

---

## Was ich für dieses Repo vorschlagen würde

1. **Windows:** CI-Schritt um `-nsis` erweitern → `*-setup.exe` an die GitHub Release hängen  
2. **macOS:** zusätzlich DMG neben dem Zip; Signing/Notarize später  
3. **Linux:** AppImage (und ggf. `.deb`); Flatpak Phase 2  
4. `wails.json` `info` + Versionsnummer aus Git-Tag füttern  

Technisch alles machbar mit eurem Stack (Wails v2 + vorhandene `build/`-Struktur). Der größte „Produkt“-Aufwand ist Signing (Windows + Apple), nicht AppImage/NSIS/DMG selbst.

Wenn du das umsetzen lassen willst: in **Agent mode** wechseln — dann kann man CI + Packaging schrittweise einbauen.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build a (thin) AppImage from the Wails Linux binary.
# Requires: appimagetool on PATH, binary linked against system WebKitGTK.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
BINARY="${1:-$ROOT/build/bin/gotify-desktop}"
OUT_DIR="${2:-$ROOT/dist}"
ARCH_NAME="${3:-linux-amd64}"
VERSION="${APP_VERSION:-0.0.0}"

if [[ ! -x "$BINARY" && ! -f "$BINARY" ]]; then
  echo "binary not found: $BINARY" >&2
  exit 1
fi

WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORKDIR"' EXIT

APPDIR="$WORKDIR/GotifyDesktop.AppDir"
mkdir -p \
  "$APPDIR/usr/bin" \
  "$APPDIR/usr/share/applications" \
  "$APPDIR/usr/share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps"

OUT_DIR="${2:-$ROOT/dist}"

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GO_VERSION: "1.25.x"
  NODE_VERSION: "24"
  NODE_OPTIONS: "--max-old-space-size=4096"
  WAILS_VERSION: "v2.17.0"

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum

      # main.go embeds frontend/dist; keep a placeholder so `go test ./...` can compile.
      - name: Ensure frontend embed path exists
        run: |
          mkdir -p frontend/dist
          printf '%s\n' '<!doctype html><title>gotify-desktop</title>' > frontend/dist/index.html

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: go test ./...

  build:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.name }})
    needs: test
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: linux-amd64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            platform: linux/amd64
            wails_tags: webkit2_41
            artifact: gotify-desktop
          - name: windows-amd64
            os: windows-latest
            platform: windows/amd64
            wails_tags: ""
            artifact: gotify-desktop.exe
          # arm64-only: avoids long universal link; systray is stubbed on darwin (Wails conflict).
          - name: darwin-arm64
            os: macos-latest
            platform: darwin/arm64
            wails_tags: ""
            artifact: gotify-desktop.app

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version: ${{ env.GO_VERSION }}
          cache-dependency-path: go.sum

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Resolve app version
        id: ver
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF}" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
            echo "version=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "version=0.0.0-dev.${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Patch wails.json productVersion
        shell: bash
        env:
          APP_VERSION: ${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          chmod +x packaging/set-version.sh
          ./packaging/set-version.sh

      - name: Install Linux dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            fuse libfuse2 wget

      - name: Install NSIS (Windows installer)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: choco install nsis -y --no-progress

      - name: Install Wails CLI
        run: go install github.com/wailsapp/wails/v2/cmd/wails@${{ env.WAILS_VERSION }}

      - name: Drop Linux-only build tags on Windows/macOS
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          path = Path("wails.json")
          data = json.loads(path.read_text())
          data.pop("build:tags", None)
          path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n")
          PY

      - name: Build (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: wails build -platform "${{ matrix.platform }}" -clean -tags "${{ matrix.wails_tags }}"

      - name: Build + NSIS installer (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export PATH="/c/Program Files (x86)/NSIS:/c/Program Files/NSIS:$PATH"
          wails build -platform "${{ matrix.platform }}" -clean -nsis
          ls -la build/bin/

      - name: Build (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: wails build -platform "${{ matrix.platform }}" -clean

      - name: Package Linux AppImage
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        env:
          APP_VERSION: ${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist tools
          curl -fsSL -o tools/appimagetool \
            https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/download/continuous/appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage
          chmod +x tools/appimagetool packaging/linux/build-appimage.sh
          # Extract on CI (FUSE often unavailable in containers).
          cd tools && ./appimagetool --appimage-extract && cd ..
          export PATH="$PWD/tools/squashfs-root/usr/bin:$PATH"
          ./packaging/linux/build-appimage.sh \
            "build/bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}" \
            dist \
            "${{ matrix.name }}"
          cp "build/bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}" "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}"
          chmod +x "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}"

      - name: Package Windows artifacts
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          cp "build/bin/${{ matrix.artifact }}" "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}.exe"
          # Wails NSIS OutFile: ${INFO_PROJECTNAME}-${ARCH}-installer.exe
          if [[ -f build/bin/gotify-desktop-amd64-installer.exe ]]; then
            cp build/bin/gotify-desktop-amd64-installer.exe \
              "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}-setup.exe"
          else
            echo "NSIS installer missing; listing build/bin:" >&2
            ls -la build/bin/ >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Package macOS zip + DMG
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          ditto -c -k --sequesterRsrc --keepParent build/bin/gotify-desktop.app \
            "dist/gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}.zip"
          chmod +x packaging/darwin/build-dmg.sh
          ./packaging/darwin/build-dmg.sh \
            build/bin/gotify-desktop.app \
            dist \
            "${{ matrix.name }}"

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: gotify-desktop-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    name: Release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Download all build artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: release-assets
          pattern: gotify-desktop-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: release-assets/*
          generate_release_notes: true
          body: |
            ## Downloads
            | Platform | Files |
            |----------|--------|
            | Windows | `gotify-desktop-windows-amd64-setup.exe` (NSIS), `.exe` |
            | Linux | `gotify-desktop-linux-amd64.AppImage`, binary |
            | macOS | `gotify-desktop-darwin-arm64.dmg`, `.zip` |

            Linux AppImage needs WebKitGTK 4.1 on the host (`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`).
            macOS builds are unsigned (Gatekeeper may warn until notarized).
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on pushes/PRs to `main` and on version tags:

1. Unit tests
2. Native builds for **Linux**, **Windows**, and **macOS** (arm64)

```bash
# Windows (with NSIS on PATH)

./packaging/linux/build-appimage.sh build/bin/gotify-desktop dist linux-amd64

# macOS DMG (after wails build)
./packaging/darwin/build-dmg.sh build/bin/gotify-desktop.app dist darwin-arm64
```

Pushing a version tag creates a GitHub Release:

```bash
git tag v0.1.9
git push origin v0.1.9
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Patch productVersion in wails.json (run from repo root).
# APP_VERSION may be "0.1.9", "v0.1.9", or a CI dev string.
# NSIS VIProductVersion requires numeric X.Y.Z — non-release builds use 0.0.0.
set -euo pipefail

RAW="${APP_VERSION:-${1:-}}"
if [[ -z "$RAW" ]]; then
  echo "usage: APP_VERSION=0.1.9 $0" >&2
  exit 1
fi
VERSION="${RAW#v}"

# Strip pre-release / metadata so NSIS and Windows version resources stay valid.
NUMERIC="$(printf '%s' "$VERSION" | sed -E 's/[^0-9].*$//')"
if [[ ! "$NUMERIC" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+){0,3}$ ]]; then
  NUMERIC="0.0.0"
fi
# Ensure at least major.minor.patch
IFS=. read -r A B C _ <<< "${NUMERIC}..."
A="${A:-0}"; B="${B:-0}"; C="${C:-0}"
NUMERIC="${A}.${B}.${C}"

WAILS_JSON="${WAILS_JSON:-wails.json}"
if [[ ! -f "$WAILS_JSON" ]]; then
  echo "wails.json not found at: $WAILS_JSON (cwd=$(pwd))" >&2
  exit 1
fi

export NUMERIC VERSION WAILS_JSON
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

path = Path(os.environ["WAILS_JSON"])
data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
info = data.setdefault("info", {})
info["productVersion"] = os.environ["NUMERIC"]
path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print(f"wails.json productVersion={os.environ['NUMERIC']} (from {os.environ['VERSION']})")
PY

content.text:
Ja — **vor allem Windows und macOS**. Linux ist optional.

### Windows (NSIS / `.exe`) — stark empfohlen
Ohne Signatur: SmartScreen („unbekannter Herausgeber“), oft blockiert bis man „Weitere Informationen“ klickt.  
Mit **Authenticode** (Code Signing Certificate, z. B. Sectigo/DigiCert, heute oft **OV + Hardware/Cloud-HSM**):

- `signtool` auf `.exe` und Setup
- Timestamp-Server (bleibt nach Zertifikat-Ablauf gültig)
- In eurer `project.nsi` sind `#finalize` / `#uninstfinalize` schon als Platzhalter vorgesehen

**Lohnt sich**, sobald Fremde die App von GitHub laden sollen.

### macOS (DMG / `.app`) — praktisch Pflicht für „fremde“ Macs
Ohne **Developer ID + Notarisierung**: Gatekeeper-Warnung, teils nur per Rechtsklick → Öffnen.  
Ablauf: Apple Developer Program → `codesign` → `notarytool` → `stapler`.

**Lohnt sich**, sobald Nicht-Entwickler macOS-Builds nutzen sollen.

### Linux (AppImage / Binary) — meist verzichtbar
Kein vergleichbares OS-Default-Gatekeeper. Sinnvoll eher:

- **Checksums** (`SHA256SUMS`) im Release
- optional GPG-Signatur der Checksums / des AppImages
- bei Flatpak später: Flathub signiert ohnehin anders

Für den aktuellen Stand (GitHub Releases, AppImage + Binary) reichen oft **SHA256-Dateien**.

---

**Priorität für euch:**  
1. Windows Authenticode  
2. macOS Developer ID + Notarize  
3. Linux: SHA256(+ optional GPG)

Kosten grob: Windows-Zertifikat oft dreistellig €/Jahr (+ ggf. HSM/Cloud); Apple Developer ~99 $/Jahr.

Wenn du willst, können wir als Nächstes CI-Hooks für Signing vorbereiten (Secrets, `signtool`/`codesign`, Checksums) — ohne dass Zertifikate schon da sein müssen.

<timestamp>Saturday, Oct 31, 2026, 10:30 AM (UTC+1)</timestamp>
<user_query>
ich dachte eher an self signed
</user_query>

Self-signed bringt für euren Use-Case **kaum Nutzen** — eher Verwirrung.

### Windows
Self-signed Authenticode:
- SmartScreen bleibt rot/gelb („unbekannter Herausgeber“)
- Nutzer müssten euer Root-Zertifikat **manuell** in den Trust-Store legen — unrealistisch für GitHub-Downloads
- Wirkt fast wie unsigniert, nur mit Extra-Schritten

→ Self-signed lohnt sich höchstens intern (eigene PCs, Lab).

### macOS
Self-signed / ad-hoc (`codesign -s -`):
- Gatekeeper akzeptiert das **nicht** für fremde Macs
- Notarisierung geht **nur** mit Apple Developer ID

→ Self-signed hilft Endnutzern nicht.

### Linux
Hier ist Self-signed/GPG sinnvoller:
- AppImage oder Release mit **GPG** signieren + `SHA256SUMS`
- Nutzer, die deinen Public Key kennen, können verifizieren
- Kein OS-„Trust Store“-Zwang wie bei Win/macOS

---

**Fazit:** Self-signed ersetzt kein Käufe-Zertifikat auf Windows/macOS. Für öffentliche Releases entweder:
- **ungesignet** lassen + `SHA256SUMS` (pragmatisch), oder  
- später **echte** Zertifikate, oder  
- Linux zusätzlich **GPG + Checksums**.

Self-signed Windows/macOS würde ich nicht einbauen — es suggeriert Sicherheit, ohne die Warnungen wegzunehmen.

<available_subagent_types>
Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. Use when searching for a keyword or file and not confident you'll find the match quickly.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- cursor-guide: Read Cursor product documentation to answer questions about how Cursor Desktop, IDE, CLI, Cloud Agents, Bugbot, and other features work. Use when the user asks 'In Cursor, how do I...?' or similar questions about Cursor products.
- ci-investigator: Investigate a single failing PR CI check and return a short root-cause summary. Use when the user asks to summarize, explain, diagnose, or investigate a specific failed check from a pull request.
- bugbot: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a Bugbot-like review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Bugbot". Launch exactly one Bugbot subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\", \"natural language\">\nChange Description: ...\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Change Description` only when `Diff` is `natural language`, formatting it as one block per changed file (a `<path> (added|modified|deleted|renamed)` header followed by bullets of what changed, mentioning line numbers or ranges inline where helpful), and only use `natural language` as a last resort after a regular diff-based review failed because the diff could not be computed; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- security-review: Use only when the user *explicitly* asks for a security review of local code changes. When launching this subagent, set the Task description to exactly "Security Review". Launch exactly one security-review subagent with `run_in_background: false` unless the user explicitly asks to run in background. Use this fixed prompt form: "Full Repository Path: ...\nDiff: <one of: \"branch changes\", \"uncommitted changes\">\nCustom Instructions: ..."; default to `Diff: branch changes`; include `Custom Instructions` only when the user gave specific review instructions. This subagent is single-shot and does not support `resume`; always launch a fresh subagent instead.
- best-of-n-runner: Run a task in an isolated git worktree. Each best-of-n-runner gets its own branch and working directory. Use for best-of-N parallel attempts or isolated experiments.
- gsd-advisor-researcher: "Researches a single gray area decision and returns a structured comparison table with rationale. Spawned by discuss-phase advisor mode."
- gsd-assumptions-analyzer: "Deeply analyzes codebase for a phase and returns structured assumptions with evidence. Spawned by discuss-phase assumptions mode."
- gsd-codebase-mapper: "Explores codebase and writes structured analysis documents. Spawned by map-codebase with a focus area (tech, arch, quality, concerns). Writes documents directly to reduce orchestrator context load."
- gsd-debugger: "Investigates bugs using scientific method, manages debug sessions, handles checkpoints. Spawned by /gsd-debug orchestrator."
- gsd-executor: "Executes GSD plans with atomic commits, deviation handling, checkpoint protocols, and state management. Spawned by execute-phase orchestrator or execute-plan command."
- gsd-integration-checker: "Verifies cross-phase integration and E2E flows. Checks that phases connect properly and user workflows complete end-to-end."
- gsd-nyquist-auditor: "Fills Nyquist validation gaps by generating tests and verifying coverage for phase requirements"
- gsd-phase-researcher: "Researches how to implement a phase before planning. Produces RESEARCH.md consumed by gsd-planner. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator."
- gsd-plan-checker: "Verifies plans will achieve phase goal before execution. Goal-backward analysis of plan quality. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator."
- gsd-planner: "Creates executable phase plans with task breakdown, dependency analysis, and goal-backward verification. Spawned by /gsd-plan-phase orchestrator."
- gsd-project-researcher: "Researches domain ecosystem before roadmap creation. Produces files in .planning/research/ consumed during roadmap creation. Spawned by /gsd-new-project or /gsd-new-milestone orchestrators."
- gsd-research-synthesizer: "Synthesizes research outputs from parallel researcher agents into SUMMARY.md. Spawned by /gsd-new-project after 4 researcher agents complete."
- gsd-roadmapper: "Creates project roadmaps with phase breakdown, requirement mapping, success criteria derivation, and coverage validation. Spawned by /gsd-new-project orchestrator."
- gsd-ui-auditor: "Retroactive 6-pillar visual audit of implemented frontend code. Produces scored UI-REVIEW.md. Spawned by /gsd-ui-review orchestrator."
- gsd-ui-checker: "Validates UI-SPEC.md design contracts against 6 quality dimensions. Produces BLOCK/FLAG/PASS verdicts. Spawned by /gsd-ui-phase orchestrator."
- gsd-ui-researcher: "Produces UI-SPEC.md design contract for frontend phases. Reads upstream artifacts, detects design system state, asks only unanswered questions. Spawned by /gsd-ui-phase orchestrator."
- gsd-user-profiler: "Analyzes extracted session messages across 8 behavioral dimensions to produce a scored developer profile with confidence levels and evidence. Spawned by profile orchestration workflows."
- gsd-verifier: "Verifies phase goal achievement through goal-backward analysis. Checks codebase delivers what phase promised, not just that tasks completed. Creates VERIFICATION.md report."
</available_subagent_types>

<dynamic_tools>
You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

Available dynamic tool namespaces:

<dynamic_tool_namespaces>
<namespace name="cursor-ide-browser" tools="browser_navigate, browser_snapshot, browser_click, browser_mouse_click_xy, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, browser_drag, browser_get_bounding_box, browser_highlight, browser_tabs, browser_cdp, browser_take_screenshot, browser_lock" namespaceUseInstructions="The cursor-ide-browser MCP server provides a Cursor-owned browser tab plus a raw Chrome DevTools Protocol command tool.

CORE WORKFLOW:
1. Start by understanding the user's goal and what success looks like on the page.
2. Use browser_tabs with action "list" to inspect open tabs and URLs before acting.
3. Use browser_navigate to create or navigate the target tab. Omit the position parameter for background automation so focus is preserved.
4. Use browser_lock before longer automation on an existing tab, then browser_lock with action "unlock" when finished.
5. Use browser_snapshot for accessibility context and browser_take_screenshot for visual verification.
6. Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for page interactions.
7. Use browser_highlight and browser_get_bounding_box for visual grounding and coordinate diagnostics.
8. Use browser_cdp for page inspection, profiling, runtime evaluation, DOM/CSS queries, and performance data.

AVOID RABBIT HOLES:
1. Do not repeat the same failing action more than once without new evidence such as a fresh snapshot, a different ref, a changed page state, or a clear new hypothesis.
2. IMPORTANT: If four attempts fail or progress stalls, stop acting and report what you observed, what blocked progress, and the most likely next step.
3. Prefer gathering evidence over brute force. If the page is confusing, use browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot, or CDP inspection before trying more actions.
4. If you encounter a blocker such as login, passkey/manual user interaction, permissions, captchas, destructive confirmations, missing data, or an unexpected state, stop and report it instead of improvising repeated actions.
5. Do not get stuck in wait-action-wait loops. Every retry should be justified by something newly observed.

CRITICAL - Lock/unlock workflow:
1. browser_lock requires an existing browser tab - you CANNOT call browser_lock with action: "lock" before browser_navigate
2. Correct order: browser_navigate -> browser_lock({ action: "lock" }) -> (interactions) -> browser_lock({ action: "unlock" })
3. If a browser tab already exists (check with browser_tabs list), call browser_lock with action: "lock" FIRST before any interactions
4. Only call browser_lock with action: "unlock" when completely done with ALL browser operations for this turn

IMPORTANT - Waiting strategy:
When waiting for page changes, prefer short CDP polling loops with Runtime.evaluate, DOM queries, Page lifecycle signals, or browser_snapshot checks rather than a single long wait.

CDP USAGE:
- Use browser_cdp with a DevTools Protocol method and params object, for example Runtime.evaluate, DOM.getDocument, CSS.getComputedStyleForNode, Profiler.start/stop, Performance.getMetrics, Log.enable, and Network.enable.
- Do not use browser_cdp with CDP Input.* methods. They are denied because they are focus-sensitive in Electron webviews and can route input to Cursor UI instead of the browser page.
- Use browser_click, browser_type, browser_fill, browser_select_option, browser_press_key, browser_scroll, and browser_drag for clicks, typing, filling inputs, selecting options, keyboard actions, scrolling, and drag-and-drop.
- Use Runtime.evaluate for advanced DOM-scoped interactions that the dedicated browser tools do not cover.
- For profiling, call Profiler.enable, Profiler.start, reproduce the behavior, then Profiler.stop. The profile is saved to a file and returned as a log_file; read that file only when you need to inspect details.
- For JavaScript evaluation, prefer Runtime.evaluate with returnByValue when possible.
- Device emulation you set with Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled, or Emulation.setUserAgentOverride (for example for a phone-sized screenshot) lasts only for the current turn: it is cleared when your turn ends, and the user can reset it from the browser tab at any time. Send Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride yourself once you are done with it within a turn.
- Some browser-wide or sensitive CDP methods are denied, especially cookie, storage, permission, download, target-management, filesystem-backed file-input commands, system-level commands, and CDP navigation/history navigation commands.
- Large CDP responses are saved to files instead of being inlined. Prefer using the returned file path over immediately stuffing large payloads into context; read focused sections only when needed.

VISION:
- browser_take_screenshot attaches an image result that the model can inspect. CDP Page.captureScreenshot returns data inside JSON and should not replace browser_take_screenshot when visual verification is needed.

NOTES:
- browser_snapshot returns snapshot YAML and is the main source of truth for page structure.
- Refs are opaque handles tied to the latest browser_snapshot for that tab.
- Iframe content is not accessible - only elements outside iframes can be interacted with.
- When you stop to report a blocker, include the current page, the target you were trying to reach, the blocker you observed, and the best next action. If the blocker requires manual user interaction, ask the user to take over at that point rather than assuming it in advance." source="mcp" />

input.contents:
# Notification history — design

Date: 2026-10-31  
Status: approved for planning

## Goal

Users can open a scrollable list of recent notifications from the tray (or macOS app menu), with timestamps. Entries persist across restarts. Each entry can be copied to the clipboard as Markdown.

## Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Presentation | Dedicated in-app view (`history`), not tray submenu items |
| Persistence | On disk next to config; ring buffer max **100** |
| Default capture mode | **Toasts only** (`history_mode=toasts`) |
| Mode control | Toggle in the history view only (not setup form) |
| Modes | `toasts` = only messages that went through the desktop toast path; `all` = every stream message that reaches `handleMessage` after existing dedup/`min_priority` gates for toast path — see capture rules below |
| Copy format | Markdown: `**{title}**\n{body}\n\n_{timestamp}_` (omit title line if empty); local timestamp |
| Approach | Local ring buffer + JSON file + Wails UI (not Gotify REST, not `notify.log`) |

## Architecture

### Package `internal/history`

Responsibilities:

- In-memory list (newest first) capped at 100
- Load/save `history.json` in the same directory as `config.json`
- Thread-safe append + trim
- Pure helper to format an entry as Markdown for clipboard

Entry fields:

- `id` (string; Gotify message id or synthetic)
- `title`, `body` (string)
- `priority` (int)
- `app_id` (uint)
- `received_at` (RFC3339, local receive time)
- `notified` (bool — `true` if a desktop toast was attempted/shown for this entry)

Corrupt or missing file → treat as empty list and recreate on next save. Save errors are logged; they must not break the stream.

### Config

Add to `config.Config`:

- `history_mode` — `"toasts"` (default) or `"all"`

Persisted when the user toggles the control in the history UI.

### Capture rules (`handleMessage`)

Existing filters stay first: `min_priority`, `last_message_id` dedup. Messages filtered out there never enter history.

Then:

1. Decide whether this message triggers a toast (current toast path).
2. If toast: show notification as today; append history entry with `notified=true`.
3. If no toast:
   - `history_mode=all` → append with `notified=false`
   - `history_mode=toasts` → do not append

`TestNotification` appends a history entry with `notified=true`.

**Display filter:** The UI lists all stored entries when mode is `all`, and only `notified=true` when mode is `toasts`. Changing mode does not rewrite old rows; it changes future capture and the filter applied when reading for display.

### App / tray wiring

- Tray + app menu: **Recent notifications** / localized equivalent → `ShowWindow` + switch view to `history`
- Wails bindings:
  - `GetNotificationHistory() []HistoryEntry` (already filtered for current mode)
  - `GetHistoryMode() string` / `SetHistoryMode(mode string)`
  - `ClearNotificationHistory()`
  - Optional: `FormatNotificationMarkdown(id)` if clipboard is done in Go; otherwise format in frontend from entry fields
- Event `history-updated` after append/clear so an open history view refreshes
- View enum extended: `"setup" | "gotify" | "history"`

Clipboard: prefer frontend `navigator.clipboard.writeText` with the agreed Markdown; brief “Copied” feedback. Fallback to Wails clipboard API only if the webview blocks clipboard.

## UI

- Header: back (to gotify if configured, else setup), mode toggle (toasts / all), clear action
- Scrollable list, newest first
- Row: local timestamp, title, body (readable wrap), small copy button
- Empty state when no matching entries
- i18n keys in `en` / `de` / `fr` / `es` for menu, tray, headings, toggle, clear, copy, empty, copied

macOS: same entry in the native application menu (systray disabled).

## Error handling

- History I/O failures: log only
- Unknown `history_mode` on load: treat as `toasts`
- Clipboard failure: show short error in UI; do not crash

## Testing

- Ring buffer trims to 100 (oldest dropped)
- Load/save round-trip
- Display filter: `toasts` vs `all` with mixed `notified` flags
- Markdown helper matches the locked format
- Mode persistence via config (unit or thin app-level test where practical)

## Out of scope

- Fetching history from Gotify HTTP API
- Click-to-open deep link into Gotify message detail
- Syncing history across machines
- Unlimited retention or user-configurable cap (fixed 100)

## Success criteria

- Tray/menu opens a scrollable history view with timestamps
- Up to 100 entries survive restart
- Toggle switches toasts-only vs all (default toasts)
- Each row copies Markdown in the agreed format
- Existing toast/stream behavior unchanged aside from history side effects

# Persistent window geometry — design

Date: 2026-10-31  
Status: approved for planning

## Goal

The native Gotify Desktop window remembers **size**, **position**, and **maximised** state across restarts and hide-to-tray cycles.

## Decisions (locked)

| Topic | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| What | Native app window (not the Gotify iframe) |
| Fields | Width, height, x, y, maximised |
| Storage | `config.json` (same file as session settings) |
| When to save | Debounced while moving/resizing **and** on hide-to-tray / quit |
| First run | Current defaults: 1100×800, OS default position, not maximised |
| Approach | Wails runtime get/set + config fields |

## Config fields

Optional keys on `config.Config` (JSON):

- `window_width` / `window_height` (int; 0 or missing = use app defaults)
- `window_x` / `window_y` (int; use a presence flag or sentinel so `0,0` is valid — prefer explicit `window_geometry_set bool` or store only when user has moved once; **implementation:** treat width/height `<=0` as unset; for position use `window_pos_set bool` `json:"window_pos_set,omitempty"` so `0,0` can be saved)
- `window_maximised` (bool)

Defaults in code remain `Width: 1100`, `Height: 800`, `MinWidth: 640`, `MinHeight: 480` in `main.go`.

## Restore

After Wails context is available (`startup` or early `domReady`):

1. If saved width/height valid (≥ mins): `WindowSetSize`
2. If `window_pos_set`: `WindowSetPosition` after a simple on-screen clamp (if clearly off-screen, skip position and let OS place)
3. If `window_maximised`: `WindowMaximise`
4. Do not force-show the window here if `StartHidden` / tray flow expects hidden start — apply geometry while hidden is OK

## Save

- Exported `SaveWindowState()` on `App`:
  - Read size, position, maximised via Wails runtime
  - If maximised: keep previously stored normal bounds when the platform reports maximised size as the full screen; if platform returns restore bounds already, persist those
  - Clamp width/height to ≥ min sizes
  - Set `window_pos_set = true`
  - Persist only if something changed
  - Log save errors; never fail the UI path
- Debounce ~400ms from the frontend (window `resize` + lightweight position polling or move-related events if available) calling `SaveWindowState`
- Also call from `beforeClose` (hide-to-tray) and shutdown/quit paths

## Out of scope

- Per-monitor DPI profile databases
- Fullscreen state (distinct from maximised)
- Remembering which virtual desktop / workspace

## Success criteria

- Resize, move, maximise → quit or hide → reopen → same geometry
- Debounced saves during interactive resize/move without noticeable UI jank
- Invalid/off-screen saved position does not leave the window unreachable
- README mentions the new config fields

Bug 1:
When a window is maximised for the first time without prior saved geometry, `MergeWindowGeometry` stores the full screen dimensions (e.g., 1920x1080 or larger on high-DPI displays) as the normal window bounds. On subsequent app launches, the window will open at this oversized dimension instead of the intended 1100×800 default. A `setInterval` is established at module load time (line 399) that polls `SaveWindowState()` every 2 seconds while the document is visible. This interval is never cleared, causing indefinite polling to continue even if the window is closed or the app shuts down. While `SaveWindowState()` includes guards (`a.ctx == nil` check) that prevent errors, the unnecessary polling continues indefinitely, creating a resource leak and potential performance degradation.

#### Desktop environment support

Having the library installed is necessary but not always sufficient. The shell must also **host** indicators:

| Desktop | Tray support |
|---------|----------------|
| **KDE Plasma** | Built-in system tray; works out of the box with SNI |
| **XFCE** | Panel → add “Status Tray Plugin” / “Indicator Plugin” |
| **MATE** | Panel → “Notification Area” / “Indicator Applet Complete” |
| **Cinnamon** | Usually works with the default panel tray |
| **GNOME (45+)** | No classic tray by default. Install an extension such as [AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support](https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/615/appindicator-support/) (`gnome-shell-extension-appindicator` on Ubuntu/Fedora) and **enable** it |
| **WSL / headless** | Often **no** tray host at all; run under a full Linux desktop session or WSLg with a DE that provides one |

Ubuntu GNOME example:

```bash
sudo apt install libayatana-appindicator3-1 gnome-shell-extension-appindicator
```

Then enable the extension (Extensions app, or GNOME Tweaks / `gnome-extensions enable …`), and log out/in if the icon still does not show.

#### Fedora / GNOME: “app vanished after login”

On a successful first connect (and whenever a saved session starts), Gotify Desktop **hides the main window and keeps running in the tray**. That is intentional — not a crash.

Under stock **Fedora Workstation (GNOME)** there is no classic system tray. Without an indicator host the window simply disappears and there is nowhere obvious to reopen it.

What to do:

1. Install runtime + extension packages (see `dnf` above).
2. Open **Extensions** (`gnome-extensions-app`) and enable **AppIndicator and KStatusNotifierItem Support**.
3. If the toggle stays greyed out, user extensions may be disabled globally — turn them on, then enable the extension:

```bash
gsettings set org.gnome.shell disable-user-extensions false
gnome-extensions enable appindicatorsupport@rgcjonas.gmail.com
```

4. Restart Gotify Desktop. The tray icon appears in the **GNOME top bar** (top-right, near network/volume/clock) — not in the Activities app grid.
5. Use the tray menu (**Open window** / **Quit**). To force a restart from a terminal:

```bash
pkill -f gotify-desktop; gotify-desktop &
```

Log out/in once if the icon still does not appear after enabling the extension.

content.text:
Ja — unter **Wayland** (CachyOS) sind vor allem diese Punkte erwartbar:

**Fensterposition**  
Wayland liefert Clients oft keine echte Bildschirmposition (`gtk_window_get_position` → `0,0`). Größe und Maximiert sollten gehen; die gespeicherte Position wirkt oft nicht oder landet immer „oben links / Compositor-Default“. Das steht schon in der README.

**Tray**  
Abhängig von der Shell:
- **KDE Plasma (Wayland):** meist unauffällig (SNI eingebaut)
- **Hyprland / Sway / andere WLs:** Tray nur mit Panel + SNI-Host (z. B. Waybar `tray`, oder vergleichbar) — sonst wieder „Fenster weg nach Login“
- **GNOME Wayland:** wie unter Fedora — AppIndicator-Extension nötig

**Benachrichtigungen**  
Über Portals (`xdg-desktop-portal` + Backend für deine Session). Ohne passendes Portal: Fallback/`Notify: Fallback` oder stille Toasts. Unter Plasma/GNOME meist ok, unter reinem Hyprland oft Extra-Setup.

**Autostart**  
XDG-Autostart funktioniert oft, Start vor fertigem Wayland-Portal kann Tray/Notify verzögern oder einmal fehlschlagen — App neu starten hilft.

**Sonst eher unkritisch**  
WebView/Login/Stream sollten mit GTK3+WebKitGTK unter Wayland laufen. Selten: Clipboard/Focus-Quirks beim Kopieren aus der History.

Kurz: Am ehesten **Position ignorieren**, **Tray-Host prüfen**, **Portal für Notify**. Wenn du sagst, welche Session (Plasma / Hyprland / …), kann ich die Checkliste enger machen.

#### Wayland (e.g. CachyOS, Fedora Workstation, Plasma Wayland)

Gotify Desktop is a GTK3 / WebKitGTK / Wails app. It generally runs under Wayland, but a few behaviours differ from X11:

| Area | What to expect |
|------|----------------|
| **Window position** | Wayland often does not expose global coordinates to clients (`gtk_window_get_position` may always report `0,0`). **Size** and **maximised** still persist; restoring a previous screen position may be ignored or land at the compositor default. |
| **Tray** | Same rules as above — the compositor/shell must host Status Notifier / AppIndicator. Plasma Wayland usually works out of the box; GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension; Hyprland/Sway need a panel with a tray module. |
| **Notifications** | Desktop toasts go through `xdg-desktop-portal` and a session backend. Plasma/GNOME usually provide one; a minimal Hyprland setup may need an extra portal package or show `Notify: Fallback` / silent toasts until portals are configured. |
| **Autostart** | XDG autostart still works, but starting before the session bus / portals are ready can delay tray or notifications once — restarting the app after login fixes that. |
| **Clipboard / focus** | Occasional focus or clipboard quirks in the embedded UI (e.g. History → Copy) are possible; retry or refocus the window if a copy fails. |

```bash
echo "$XDG_SESSION_TYPE"   # expect "wayland"
echo "$WAYLAND_DISPLAY"
echo "$XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP"
```
